build.reason: The supplied recipe compiles this C target against the changed public header and links the static Expat library; the legacy setter declaration and implementation remain present. This is a static compatibility assessment, not a claim that a build was run.

input.reason: A finite UTF-8 XML input such as <a/> satisfies the target's size guard and XML_Parse's pointer and length preconditions; parse errors are handled without an existing success assertion.

lifecycle.reason: The target creates parent and namespace parsers, checks creation, conditionally uses and frees external children, then frees the parent. Reset is attempted only while a parser is live; its return value is not asserted.

control_flow.reason: Each ParseOneInput call configures the parser with XML_SetHashSalt before parsing. The complete target has no call or equivalent sequence that selects an explicit 16-byte salt.

accepted.requirement: For the parsers it creates and parses, the target must make the supported explicit 16-byte hash-salt setup reachable before parsing.
accepted.target_route: LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput creates parent and namespace parsers and, later, two possible external parsers. ParseOneInput always calls XML_SetHashSalt with one unsigned-long value before XML_Parse.
accepted.failure_condition: For finite accepted XML such as <a/> and a 16-byte entropy value with a nonzero first key word, the target has no setup that can select that value; the legacy setter sets the first word to zero.
accepted.alternative_paths: The complete entry and helper show no XML_SetHashSalt16Bytes call or alternate setup. Automatic salt generation cannot select a specified 16-byte value, and external parsers inherit the parent's setup.

source_evidence.quote:
/* Added in Expat 2.7.6. */ XML_Bool XMLCALL XML_SetHashSalt16Bytes(XML_Parser parser, const uint8_t entropy[16]);
Sets the hash salt to use for internal hash calculations. Helps in preventing DoS attacks based on predicting hash function behavior. In order to have an effect this must be called before parsing has started. Returns XML_TRUE if successful, XML_FALSE when called after XML_Parse or XML_ParseBuffer or when parser is NULL.

Note: Setting a salt that is not from a source of high quality entropy (like getentropy(3)) will make the parser vulnerable to hash flooding attacks.

Note: This call is optional, as the parser will auto-generate a new random salt value internally if no value has been set by the start of parsing.
